title: 3rd member of Canadian Armed Forces charged in kidnapping probe: Toronto police
summary: A third member of the Canadian Armed Forces, and four other people, were arrested and charged in a kidnapping probe that led to the arrest of two other members of Canada’s military reserves, Toronto…

image.caption: Police recovered at least four firearms, 2,700 rounds of ammunition and large quantities of cocaine, methamphetamine and other controlled substances during the investigation. (Keira Mahoney/CBC)

blocks.text: A third member of the Canadian Armed Forces, and four other people, were arrested and charged in a kidnapping probe that led to the arrest of two other members of Canada’s military reserves, Toronto police announced Wednesday.
2 other military reserve members, 4 civilians also arrested and charged, police say

Joe Matthews, chief superintendent with Toronto Police Services, said the accused were arrested following an investigation that started while looking into a kidnapping on July 25. Police allege the victim was confined in the car at gunpoint, handcuffed and was assaulted as suspects tried to access cryptocurrency assets.

items: 2 Canadian Armed Forces members arrested in organized crime, kidnapping probe, DND says

blocks.text: Jack Miley, a 24-year-old from Toronto and reserve member of the CAF, was arrested on Sept. 24 and is facing seven charges including kidnapping for ransom with a firearm, forcible confinement and a number of firearm charges, said Matthews.

Earlier this month, police announced Talarambage Fernando and James Moreau, both reserve members of the 7 Toronto Regiment, were arrested on Aug. 11 in relation to the same investigation. Miley is a member of a different regiment, police said Wednesday.
Four civilians were also arrested, police said.

Police recovered at least four firearms during the investigation and 2,700 rounds of ammunition, about half of them blanks, were allegedly stolen from the military. They also found large quantities of cocaine, methamphetamine and other controlled substances.

Fernando, 22, and Moreau, 29, are facing a combined total of 49 charges, police said following their arrest. The pair have since been removed from their duties and their access to military facilities and bases has been restricted, according to the Department of National Defence.

Both have been charged with kidnapping for ransom, forcible confinement, unauthorized possession of a firearm in a motor vehicle, use of a firearm during the commission of an indictable offence, and mischief interfere with property.

Matthews said it’s not clear how the seven accused all knew each other, but said that’s part of the ongoing investigation. He said there’s nothing to indicate the accused are tied to any larger organized crime circles.
